info.bio:
Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta, más conocida por su nombre artístico, Lady Gaga (Manhattan, Nueva York, 28 de marzo de 1986) es una cantante, compositora, productora musical, bailarina y pianista estadounidense. Stefani creció escuchando a bandas tales como Queen, al igual que a artistas pop como Michael Jackson y Madonna, quienes luego se convertirían en grandes influencias para ella.

En agosto de 2008, la cantante lanzó su álbum de debut

podcast.title: YouTube Record Broken (2009)
podcast.body: Lady Gaga previously held a YouTube view record that was surpassed by Mumford & Sons' "Winter Winds" on December 6, 2009. "Winter Winds" achieved 250,000 views in 12 hours, breaking Lady Gaga's record by more than 25%. "And that broke the previous record, said by Lady Gaga, by more than 25%."

podcast.title: Lost Album of the Year to The Arcade Fire (2011)
podcast.body: Lady Gaga was a nominee for Album of the Year in 2011, but The Arcade Fire's album "The Suburbs" ultimately took the prize. "In 2011, the arcade fire were shocked when their album The Suburbs took album of the Year over Eminem, Lady Gaga, Lady Antebellum and Katy Perry."

podcast.title: Social Media Dominance (2011)
podcast.body: At the peak of her chart success in 2011, Lady Gaga was identified by Rolling Stone as not only Twitter's most followed music star but also the site's most followed person overall, boasting a commanding 11 million followers. Her Facebook presence was equally massive, with 39 million likes at the time, surpassing Rihanna and Shakira. "Rolling Stone revealed that she was not only Twitter's most followed music star, but the site's most followed person period, with a commanding 11 million followers."

podcast.body: Lady Gaga attended the Hollywood premiere of the documentary "Who the F Is Arthur Fogel" in full costume, demonstrating her high regard for the concert promoter Arthur Fogel. podcast.title: Defaced Magazine Cover at Abbey Road
podcast.body: During a private tour of Abbey Road Studios, a fashion magazine featuring Lady Gaga on the cover was discovered. Someone had used a Sharpie to draw a beard and mustache on her image, found amidst vintage and new recording gear throughout the building. "There was also a fashion magazine with Lady Gaga on the cover. Someone had taken a sharpie and drawn a beard and a mustache on her."

podcast.title: Early 2010s Imperial Phase
podcast.body: Lady Gaga's imperial phase in the early 2010s was marked by her ability to leverage cultural capital, as exemplified by the success of "Born This Way." She also notably set the agenda for pop music, with many electropop and Euro dance artists of the period imitating her sound and style. "One other hallmark of Lady Gaga's early 2010s imperial phase was how she set the agenda for pop."

podcast.body: Lady Gaga has a history of routinely launching her new LPs at number one, scoring her seventh number one album debut in the year of the podcast. podcast.title: Las Vegas Residency Trend
podcast.body: Lady Gaga joined the growing number of pop stars who established Las Vegas residencies, a trend initiated by artists like Celine Dion and Britney Spears. These residencies allowed popular artists to perform to dedicated fan bases in a fixed location, contributing to Las Vegas's evolution as a diverse entertainment destination. "That led to Lady Gaga, Prince, the Backstreet Boys, Mariah Carey, Cher, Shania Twain, Bruno Mars, Adele, and dozens and dozens more."

podcast.title: Smartphone Music Video Production
podcast.body: By the end of the 2010s, Lady Gaga was among the thousands of artists creating professional-level music videos in HD and 4K using only their smartphones, demonstrating the accessibility of high-quality video production technology. "people could create pro-level productions, especially after the debut of the iPhone 11. By the end of the decade, thousands of people were making music videos in HD and 4K with just their phones that included people like Lady Gaga."

"It is now known as alioti's gaga after lady gaga, of course."

xref.title: Cultural Impact - Redefining Rock Stardom
xref.body: David Bowie profoundly changed culture by subverting the traditional meaning of a rock star, pushing music into new realms of theater and spectacle. His continuously shape-shifting style was widely imitated by artists like Madonna and Lady Gaga, and he served as a crucial inspiration for punk, new wave, post-punk, electronic, goth, industrial, and alternative movements, including bands like the Pixies, Nirvana, Nine Inch Nails, and Arcade Fire. "David Bowie irrevocably changed our culture. He began by subverting what it meant to be a rock star."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Remembering David Bowie: Part 2

xref.title: Diverse Musical Career
xref.body: Sean Lennon, the son of John Lennon and Yoko Ono, has had a varied musical career. He has been a member of multiple bands, composed scores for films, produced material for other artists, and released several solo albums. He has also collaborated with prominent figures such as Albert Hammond Jr. of The Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey. "Sean Lennon is the son of John and Yoko. He's been in a bunch of different bands, scored some films, produced material for other people, recorded a couple of albums on his own, and collaborated on records with people like Albert Hammond Jr. of the Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence and Impact
xref.body: Bowie's legacy extends beyond music, influencing image, the concert arena, fashion, film, stage, painting, museums, and career management. He was a foundational figure for genres like rock, punk, new wave, goth, industrial, electronic dance music, grunge, and indie rock, appealing to diverse artists from Lady Gaga to the Sex Pistols. "Yes, his music has been extraordinarily influential, but that's only part of it."

xref.body: Mariah Carey joined the growing number of pop stars who established Las Vegas residencies, a trend initiated by artists like Celine Dion and Britney Spears. These residencies allowed popular artists to perform to dedicated fan bases in a fixed location, contributing to Las Vegas's evolution as a diverse entertainment destination. "That led to Lady Gaga, Prince, the Backstreet Boys, Mariah Carey, Cher, Shania Twain, Bruno Mars, Adele, and dozens and dozens more."

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
xref.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."

xref.title: Smartphone Music Video Production
xref.body: Selena Gomez was one of the artists who, by the end of the 2010s, utilized smartphones like the iPhone 11 to produce high-definition music videos, showcasing how advanced mobile technology allowed for professional productions with significantly reduced budgets. "people could create pro-level productions, especially after the debut of the iPhone 11. By the end of the decade, thousands of people were making music videos in HD and 4K with just their phones that included people like Lady Gaga and Selena Gomez."

xref.title: Stewart Copeland at Arthur Fogel Documentary Party
xref.body: Stewart Copeland, a member of The Police, attended the after-party for the Hollywood premiere of the documentary "Who the F Is Arthur Fogel" at the Chateau Marmont. He was seen sitting on a couch with Lady Gaga and was described as very nice and friendly. "And at one point, I found myself quite accidentally sitting on a couch with Lady Gaga to my left and steward Copeland of the police on my right."

xref.title: Widespread Influence on Artists
xref.body: Grace Jones exerted a significant influence on a diverse range of artists, including Annie Lennox of Eurythmics, Madonna, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and Lorde. Her impact extends to the drag queen and cross-dressing scene, solidifying her status as a powerful and transformative figure. "Her influence extends not just to follow her, such as any Linux of the Arithmics, but all the way through Madonna, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and Lord."
